title: Unique extension of morphisms of finite etale covers from a smooth generic fibre
statement: Let S be integral with integrally closed local rings, c:C → S smooth with geometrically connected fibres, and q:Cη → Spec K, j:Cη → C its cartesian generic fibre, where K is the function field of S [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let πX:X → C and πY:Y → C be finite etale morphisms. Let πXη:Xη → Cη, πYη:Yη → Cη and ψX:Xη → X, ψY:Yη → Y exhibit their cartesian restrictions. Every morphism fη:Xη → Yη over Cη extends uniquely to a morphism f:X → Y over C, with ψX;f=fη;ψY. No connectedness of X or Y is required.

source.place: Tag 0BQM, proof; Tag 0EYJ, proof (extension of the action)

proof.text: If C is empty, all covers and their generic restrictions are empty, and the unique empty-scheme morphism proves the conclusion. Otherwise smoothness over a normal base makes C normal. Smooth geometrically connected nonempty fibres are geometrically integral. Smoothness is open, so the nonempty image of C in the integral base contains its generic point. Thus the generic fibre is nonempty and integral. Flatness over the integral base makes that fibre dense, so C is irreducible, hence integral. Its generic point lies in Cη, which is also normal integral.

Restrict the given fη to the generic point of C, which is also the generic point of Cη. Full faithfulness of finite etale restriction to the generic point of a normal integral scheme (0BQM) gives a unique morphism f:X → Y over C. Restrict f to Cη using the cartesian comparison maps. This restricted map and fη have equal restrictions to the generic point, so faithfulness of 0BQM applied to Cη shows equality. This is precisely ψX;f=fη;ψY. The same faithfulness on C proves uniqueness. The category in 0BQM includes disconnected finite etale covers, so no component-connectedness hypothesis is needed.
